scope: Lower-body garments only (pants, shorts, skirts, skorts). Apply per labeled item when the garment type is a bottom.

attributes.description_en: Vertical position of the waistband or natural waist seam relative to the torso, judged on the garment itself (not the model's styling).

values.definition_en: Waistband sits at or above the natural waist (near the narrowest torso point, typically at or above the navel). Visually short rise length from crotch to waistband.
Waistband sits between the natural waist and the hips (around the hip bone). Default regular rise for most trousers and skirts.
Waistband sits clearly below the natural waist, on or near the upper hip. More hip bone exposure than mid rise; longer front fly/rise area.

Waist seam or waist detail sits at the upper hip or below the hip, with the main waistline intentionally lowered (not merely low rise denim). Often seen on dresses/skirts with a seam below the natural waist.
No fixed waistband position; entire waist opening is elasticized (sweatpants, lounge pants, some paperbag waists). Do not use for only partial elastic back panels.
Waist not visible (cropped top covering waist, occluded pose, or image quality). Use only when rise cannot be judged with reasonable confidence.

labeling_rules_en: Judge the garment's waistband or waist seam, not how low the model pulls the item on the body.
For skirts without a waistband, use the waist seam where the skirt attaches to the bodice or the visible waist gathering line.
If both low_rise and drop_waist could apply, prefer drop_waist only when a deliberate lowered waist seam is a design feature; otherwise use low_rise.

attributes.description_en: Hem position along the leg (or standing length for skirts), using the longest point of the hem. Seven mutually exclusive categories.

values.definition_en: Hem at upper thigh, well above mid-thigh. Hot pants, very short shorts, micro mini skirts.
Hem around mid-thigh (between upper thigh and knee). Standard short shorts and short skirts.
Hem at or just above the knee (knee cap area). Bermuda shorts, knee-length skirts.
Hem between knee and ankle, typically mid-calf. Capri pants, cropped trousers, calf-length skirts.
Hem below the knee and above the ankle, often mid-shin. Midi skirts and long culottes that end below the knee.
Hem at or just above the ankle bone. Full-length trousers, ankle-grazing skirts.
Hem at or near the floor, covering most of the foot or shoe. Maxi skirts and extra-long trousers.

labeling_rules_en: Use the lowest hem point when the hem is asymmetric (high-low, handkerchief hem).
For skorts, judge by the longest visible hem (skirt panel) unless the product is clearly shorts-length with only a decorative overlay.
Do not confuse leg opening width (wide-leg) with length; classify by where the hem meets the leg.
When in doubt between adjacent categories, choose the category where the majority of the hem circumference falls.
